Tropical Weather Outlook

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Public Advisory Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 202034
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Fay Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
...FAY CONTINUES TO STRENGTHEN AND COULD REACH HURRICANE
STATUS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...34.4N 32.7W
ABOUT 405 MI...650 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 20 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was 
located near latitude 34.4 North, longitude 32.7 West. Fay is moving 
toward the north-northeast near 6 mph (9 km/h) this general motion 
is expected to continue through the rest of the day. Afterwards a 
turn to the southwest is expected on Monday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 65 mph (100 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Additional strengthening is forecast tonight, 
and Fay could approach hurricane intensity. A gradual weakening 
trend is expected to begin on Monday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 202035
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Sun Sep 20 2026
 
A few more convective bursts have occurred near the center of Fay in 
the last couple of hours as seen in the visible satellite imagery. 
Infrared satellite imagery indicates that some of the cloud tops 
have cooled to near -70 degrees C with the latest batch of 
convection.  The current objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS 
are in the range of 45-51 kt, and the most recent TAFB Dvorak fix 
was a T3.5/55 kt. Based on the given data, the initial intensity has 
been raised to 55 kt, on the upper end of the satellite estimates. 

The environment that Fay is located in still has moisture for 
additional convective development and an approaching mid- to 
upper-level trough should allow for Fay to further intensify for 
about 12 hours or so. Once the trough lifts on Monday, wind shear 
should increase and dry air should find its way into the cyclone. 
This will lead to a gradual weakening of Fay. The current NHC 
intensity forecast calls for Fay to become a post-tropical remnant 
low by Tuesday and then dissipate near the end of the week. The 
intensity forecast is still a little higher than the model guidance 
in the short term as Fay's structure is over performing expectations 
due to the expected baroclinic support from the trough. It is still 
possible that Fay could reach hurricane strength sometime tonight. 

Fay is still moving slowly and off toward the north-northeast, with 
the initial motion estimated around 020/5 kt. This general motion is 
expected to continue for about 12 hours or. However, a low- to 
mid-level ridge is expected to build to the north by Monday. This 
ridge in turn will force Fay to turn southwestward and gradually 
accelerate over the course of the forecast period. The current NHC 
forecast track is similiar to the previous track forecast with a few 
minor adjustments and remains in good agreement with the HCCA and 
GDMI track aids.
